• The narrative spans an original science fiction story and its sequel. Both are a popular and critical success.

  • While the original did not end in such a way that a sequel was necessary, it was implied that one was not out of the question.

  • The hero is an attractive woman who, despite seemingly having no training nor skills for the ordeals she faces and the situations into which she is thrust, manages to survive by her cunning, resourcefulness, physical prowess, and sheer will.

  • The first story is set in a large, foreboding utilitarian setting that lends a sense of claustrophobia and dread. While the sequel contains many scenes that share these attributes, its setting is a vastly more open and expansive atmosphere, enabling more scenes of fast-paced action rather than subtle tension.

  • In the first story, the heroine squares off against a computer that oversees the entire facility in which the story is set. Said computer proves not to be the benign entity that it originally seems to be.

  • After the first part of the narrative, the heroine has seemingly managed to conquer her foe. She is then put in a state of suspended animation, wakes up after a far longer span of time than was expected, and soon realizes she must face the menace once more.

  • Each story features the heroine being betrayed by someone.

  • In the first story, the heroine is betrayed by an artificial intelligence whom she considered to be a colleague of sorts.

  • In the sequel, she forms an uneasy alliance with an AI whom she has trouble trusting, given the previous betrayal.

  • Each story takes place in a massive, high-tech facility funded by a mysterious institution.

  • The institution seeks, or sought, to be able to control an entity that seemingly cannot be controlled.

  • In the first story, the betrayer is an entity created by the institution. In the sequel, the betrayer is also affiliated with the institution, and makes no effort to conceal it.

  • The climax of each story has the heroine trying to save herself while an automated countdown shows exactly how much time she has left to do so.

  • In the sequel, the heroine finally vanquishes the antagonist by getting it jettisoned into the void of space, and narrowly manages to avoid the same fate herself.

  • At the very end of the sequel, the heroine is reunited with one of the few entities with which she has formed an emotional bond during her adventures.

The Queen is technically the head of state. The Queen appoints her representative the Governor General (for non-Canadians, the Governor General is selected and recommended by our Prime Minister) which carries out most of her constitutional and ceremonial duties.

This is found on the Government of Canada's website:

The Queen of Canada continues to champion public and voluntary service around the world. Her Majesty is patron of more than 600 charities and organizations, of which 33 are in Canada. Royal Canadian Air Force
